To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new method for extracting the ENSO signal from tree rings, that this method was successful in reconstructing the winter SOI from 1706-1977, and that the reconstructed SOI was highly correlated to instrumental winter SOI and SST data.

the winter Southern Oscillaton index can be reconstructed with a high degree of skill from tree-ring data, and that the reconstructed winter SOI explains the large-scale SST anomaly pattern associated with El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO).

1) The strongest ENSO-related climate signal yet detected in any tree-ring data worldwide has been identified, and 2) This ENSO-related signal has been used to reconstruct a continuous record of the winter Southern Oscillaton index from 1706 through 1977.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a dendroclimatic technique that can be used to reconstruct past climate variability on interannual to decadal time scales.
the reconstruction of past ENSO events from precisely dated tree-ring chronology data from ENSO- sensitive regions in subtropical America and Indonesia.
the development of dendroclimatic methods and the application of those methods to the reconstruction of past climatic conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reconstruction is a reliable and useful tool for studying the history of the ENSO.

the SOI reconstruction is a robust and reliable representation of ENSO activity in the tropical Pacific Ocean during the past 300 yr, with a high degree of correspondence to independent instrumental and proxy data.
the ENSO signal is detectable in tree-rings and that the ENS0 signal can be reconstructed from tree-rings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ENSO signal has been detected in the ring widths of trees growing in ENSO-sensitive areas of the subtropics and that this signal is sufficiently large, stable, and coherent to allow its reconstruction back to 1706.
the ENSO signal is strong and detectable in tree-rings, and that the ENSOs of the past are similar to those observed during the instrumental era.
the reconstruction of the winter SOI is the first to be based on the largest sample of ENSO-sensitive tree-ring chronologies ever assembled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ENSO signal in tree-ring data is much more widespread than previously thought.
the ENSO signal in the instrumental SOI is strong and well represented in the tree-ring record.
ENSO is a very old and robust feature of the climate system.
